title: Persistence: Threads That Survive
objective: After this lesson you will be able to persist threads/messages/checkpoints in Postgres with owner columns from migration one, resume conversations exactly, and migrate conversation schemas without losing history.
why: In-memory conversations die with deploys; unowned rows leak across users; schemaless blobs rot unqueryable. Persistence design (owner columns day one, message/checkpoint tables, migration discipline) makes conversations durable, private, and evolvable — the difference between a demo with memory and a product with history.

blocks.text: Threads, messages, and checkpoints all carry **owner_id + tenant_id from the first migration** — no nullable-later, no backfill saga. Every read scopes by principal (Ch.3 predicates); every write stamps ownership server-side (never trusts client-sent owners). Retrofitting isolation rewrites history under live traffic; day-one columns never need to.

blocks.caption: Three tables, ownership everywhere, resume from checkpoints

blocks.text: Schema evolves under live threads: **additive migrations** (nullable columns, new tables) deploy freely; **breaking changes** (renames, type changes) dual-write during windows, backfill offline, then cut over. Checkpoint state JSON gets **schema versions** (v1/v2 readers coexist) — old checkpoints resume under new code via migrators, never crash on unknown shapes.

blocks.title: Own every row
blocks.note: Run it: expect t1 only, then forbidden on cross-read, then Returns. List scoping plus per-row reads — both layers, proven refused where required.

items: Owner + tenant columns from migration one on threads/messages/checkpoints; server-stamped, never client-sent
Additive migrations freely; breaking via dual-write + backfill + cutover; checkpoint JSON versioned
Resume from checkpoints with ownership verified first — no owned thread, no history

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice store and confirm list/read/refusal. (b) Add tenant-2 isolation proof (same user id, different tenant reading t1 → forbidden). (c) Write the checkpoint-version migration rule (v1 state under v2 code) in two sentences.
hints: Baseline: t1-only list, cross-user forbidden, owned read Returns.
Tenant proof: {userId:'u-a', tenantId:'t-2'} reading t1 → forbidden (tenant predicate independent of user).
Migration: version-tagged state JSON; v2 code runs v1 migrators on load (additive defaults), unknown versions quarantine, never crash.
exercise.why: List scoping (bulk), per-row reads (point), tenant independence (second axis), and version migration (evolution) are the four persistence judgments.
exercise.code: // Ownership-audit pattern: list scope + point reads + tenant axis + versioned state.

quiz.q: Owner columns added 'later when needed'. Verdict?
options: Dangerous: backfilling isolation under live traffic leaks during the gap — owner columns from migration one
quiz.explain: Isolation retrofits rewrite history under load with a leak window. Day-one columns never need backfill sagas.

quiz.q: v2 code meets v1 checkpoint state. Handling?
options: Version-tagged migrators upgrade on load; unknown versions quarantine, never crash
quiz.explain: State evolution needs readers for old shapes: migrators bridge versions, quarantine catches the unknown. Crash-on-history loses users' work.

quiz.q: Same user id, different tenant reads thread. Expected?
options: Forbidden: tenant predicate independent of user — cross-tenant reads refuse regardless of user match
quiz.explain: Tenant axis independent: user match without tenant match still refuses. Both predicates, always.

summary: Ownership from migration one, additive evolution with versioned checkpoints, resume with ownership verified. History durable, private, and evolvable.
